title: 2nd Matter The Criterion Of Scientific Consensus

questions.question: In a field like science or art, whose words should be trusted most when a hard issue is being discussed?
questions.answer: The words of people who truly belong to that field and know it well should be trusted most.

questions.question: Why can a very smart and successful person still fail to speak with full authority about another field?
questions.answer: Because being great in one area does not make someone an expert in every other area.

questions.question: What example is given to show that skill in one profession does not make a person an expert in another?
questions.answer: An engineer’s opinion about treating sickness is not equal to even a humble doctor’s opinion.

questions.question: What kind of philosopher is described as not reliable in spiritual matters?
questions.answer: A philosopher who is focused only on physical things and far from spiritual reality.

questions.question: Why are such philosophers said to be weak judges in matters beyond the material world?
questions.answer: Because they only trust what they can see with their eyes, so their understanding stays limited.

questions.question: In which subjects is there said to be complete agreement among many truthful people?
questions.answer: In holy and spiritual matters, especially truths about Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What is Shaykh Gilani presented as an example of in the passage?
questions.answer: He is shown as one of the truthful spiritual people who reached very high certainty and deep understanding.

questions.question: What does the passage say Shaykh Gilani did for many years?
questions.answer: He spent a long lifetime growing in spiritual worship and uncovering truths of faith.

questions.question: How does the passage compare the objections of material-focused philosophers with the agreement of the People of Truth?
questions.answer: It says their objections are tiny and weak compared with the powerful agreement of the truthful believers.

questions.question: What lesson should a student take from this passage about learning religious truth?
questions.answer: A student should listen to people who are strong in spiritual knowledge, not just to people famous in worldly subjects.

questions.question: What main idea does this passage teach about experts and knowledge?
questions.answer: It teaches that only real experts in a subject can give strong and final judgments about it.

questions.question: Can a person be very educated and still not count as an authority in another subject? Explain.
questions.answer: Yes. A person may know a lot in one field but still not have the right knowledge for another field.

questions.question: Why is an engineer used in the example about sickness?
questions.answer: To show that being highly skilled in building or design does not make someone fit to judge medical problems.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about people who are deeply attached only to the physical world?
questions.answer: It suggests they become less able to understand spiritual truths.

questions.question: How does being limited to what the eye sees harm a person’s judgment?
questions.answer: It keeps the person from recognizing realities that are not physical or visible.

questions.question: Who are called the People of Truth in this passage?
questions.answer: They are truthful spiritual people who agree on sacred matters and truths of faith.

questions.question: What special honor or high spiritual rank is mentioned about Shaykh Gilani?
questions.answer: It says he reached an extremely high spiritual state and witnessed great realities while still on earth.

questions.question: What does the mention of many People of Truth agreeing with one another help prove?
questions.answer: It helps show that spiritual truth is supported by a strong and wide agreement.

questions.question: Why are the philosophers’ denials pictured as something very small?
questions.answer: Because their claims are weak compared with the great strength of the truthful believers’ united testimony.

questions.question: If two groups speak about spiritual truth, which group does this passage guide us to trust more?
questions.answer: It guides us to trust the truthful spiritual knowers rather than philosophers trapped in material thinking.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is needed before a person can speak firmly about a subject?
questions.answer: The person must be trained and grounded in that subject itself.

questions.question: Why are outside opinions not counted as part of the learned agreement of a field?
questions.answer: Because people outside the field do not have the proper authority or depth of knowledge in it.

questions.question: What comparison is made between a famous engineer and a simple doctor?
questions.answer: The simple doctor’s judgment about illness is worth more than the engineer’s in that matter.

questions.question: What weakness is described in a philosopher who is buried in material things?
questions.answer: Such a philosopher grows distant from spiritual realities and becomes dull toward them.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the philosopher’s mind when it comes to unseen matters?
questions.answer: It describes the mind as restricted and unable to go beyond what the eyes can notice.

questions.question: What kinds of topics are said to have full agreement among countless truthful people?
questions.answer: Sacred and spiritual topics, including belief in Divine oneness.

questions.question: Why is Shaykh Gilani mentioned by name?
questions.answer: He is named as a strong example of a person with great spiritual experience and certainty.

questions.question: What three things are said about Shaykh Gilani’s spiritual path?
questions.answer: He saw very high realities, spent many years in spiritual growth, and uncovered truths of faith at different levels of certainty.

questions.question: What image is used to compare strong truth with weak denial?
questions.answer: Weak denial is compared to a tiny insect sound, while truth is compared to a loud stormy sound.

questions.question: What feeling about faith does this comparison try to give the reader?
questions.answer: It tries to give confidence that the truth is powerful and that weak objections should not shake a believer.

questions.question: What rule about knowledge is taught at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: A person must belong to a field to speak decisively about its difficult questions.

questions.question: Why are impressive titles or achievements alone not enough in this passage?
questions.answer: Because true authority depends on the right kind of knowledge, not just fame or success.

questions.question: How does the illness example help the reader understand the rule?
questions.answer: It shows that even a great person in one field cannot replace a real expert in another field.

questions.question: What happens to a philosopher who keeps turning only toward physical things, according to the passage?
questions.answer: He becomes farther from spiritual understanding and less able to sense higher truths.

questions.question: What part of reality do such philosophers focus on too much?
questions.answer: They focus too much on the material side of life.

questions.question: In what matters do the People of Truth stand together?
questions.answer: They stand together in sacred truths and teachings about Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the number of these truthful people?
questions.answer: It says they are extremely many, reaching into the hundreds of thousands.

questions.question: How is Shaykh Gilani described to show his trustworthiness in spiritual matters?
questions.answer: He is described as someone with great spiritual vision, long years of effort, and deep certainty in faith.

questions.question: When philosophers object to these truths, how much weight does the passage give their objections?
questions.answer: It gives them very little weight.

questions.question: What is the main message about who to follow in spiritual questions?
questions.answer: The main message is to follow those with true spiritual knowledge and proven truthfulness.

questions.question: What does the passage say about people who stand outside a science or art?
questions.answer: It says they cannot give final and fully reliable judgments about that field.

questions.question: Why are their judgments not accepted as final in that field?
questions.answer: Because they do not have the special knowledge and experience of its true scholars.

questions.question: What profession is better able to judge a sickness: engineering or medicine?
questions.answer: Medicine is better able to judge a sickness.

questions.question: What is the point of comparing an engineer with a physician?
questions.answer: The point is that the right expertise matters more than status.

questions.question: What kind of thinker is criticized in the passage?
questions.answer: A thinker who is absorbed only in physical things and cut off from spiritual understanding.

questions.question: Why are such thinkers said to be unfit for judging spiritual matters?
questions.answer: Because spiritual matters go beyond what can be touched or seen, and their thinking stays stuck in the material world.

questions.question: What group is said to agree fully on sacred truths?
questions.answer: The truthful spiritual people agree fully on those truths.

questions.question: What qualities of Shaykh Gilani are mentioned to support this point?
questions.answer: His high spiritual vision, long years of worshipful striving, and deep certainty are mentioned.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the strength of united spiritual testimony?
questions.answer: It suggests that it is strong, weighty, and far greater than the denials of material-minded philosophers.

questions.question: If a Muslim student hears a spiritual question, what wise habit does this passage encourage?
questions.answer: It encourages the student to learn from trustworthy people of faith and knowledge in that area.

questions.question: What should decide whether a person’s opinion is strong in a subject?
questions.answer: Their real knowledge and standing in that subject should decide it.

questions.question: Does being important in one area automatically make someone an authority in all areas?
questions.answer: No. Authority in one area does not automatically carry over to every other area.

questions.question: Which is more dependable for curing illness in the example: the view of a top engineer or the view of a low-ranking doctor?
questions.answer: The view of the low-ranking doctor is more dependable.

questions.question: What kind of limits are placed on the philosopher described in the passage?
questions.answer: His understanding is limited by his attention to only physical and visible things.

questions.question: Why do these limits matter in discussions about the soul and sacred truth?
questions.answer: Because those discussions include realities beyond matter, and such a person is not prepared to judge them well.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the agreement of the People of Truth on Divine unity?
questions.answer: It says they are in full agreement on it.

questions.question: Why is a well-known spiritual guide mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: To give an example of someone who had deep spiritual knowledge and certainty.

questions.question: What shows that this guide had serious spiritual experience?
questions.answer: He spent many years in spiritual progress and came to know truths of faith at very high levels.

questions.question: How are the denials of materialist philosophers compared to the testimony of the People of Truth?
questions.answer: They are compared to a very faint sound next to a powerful and overwhelming one.

questions.question: What overall conclusion does the passage want the reader to reach?
questions.answer: The reader should understand that spiritual truth should be learned from trustworthy spiritual knowers, not from people limited to the material world.
